steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
This image's hitch mill is `/app/bin/twinefuse`. Feed `sew` a yarn path and a destination directory: it must write `rows.ndjson` and `hitch.idx` there. Column meanings sit in `/app/millnote/LAY.txt`. Ops bookmark a hitch token off a row, then look that token up in `hitch.idx` to recover the same id set. Sewing `/app/cordbay/eve.yarn` into `/app/dockurn` still groups those ids, yet about one hitch token in five changes when a separate OS invocation sews eve again, and the bookmark goes dead. Pair files under `/app/aliascue` join tokens that never share a dump line. Package list: `/app/millnote/ROUTE.txt`. Hull identity: `/app/millnote/HULL.txt`. The mill binary begins with bytes `\x7fELF`.

The packages named from `/app/millnote/ROUTE.txt` need source fixes under `/app`. `sew` of eve must refresh `/app/dockurn/rows.ndjson` and `/app/dockurn/hitch.idx`. Two separate OS invocations sewing eve must agree byte-for-byte on both files. `/app/cordbay/morn.yarn` has the same ids and tokens in another order; morn sew into `/app/dockurn/mornbox` must refresh `/app/dockurn/mornbox/rows.ndjson` and `/app/dockurn/mornbox/hitch.idx` and keep the same hitch token per id as eve. Yarns not already sitting in `/app/cordbay` must keep that hitch-to-id rule. A pair file whose origin field is `scrapped` must make `sew` exit non-zero with `/app/dockurn/berth.ok` false (absent). A successful sew writes `/app/dockurn/berth.ok`. Manual dockurn writes are insufficient; sew must regenerate the artifacts. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/twinefuse sew`. Agent `/app/bin/twinefuse` must sew the same `rows.ndjson` and `hitch.idx` as the throwaway mill in `/app/millnote/HULL.txt`.

Analysis: The visible code confirms multiple defects: map iteration randomizes row/index order; IDs within groups are unsorted; pair loading appears to ignore scrapped files rather than reject them and may add only the left token without joining; union-find marking likely depends on union/root order. We need inspect the omitted portions exactly before patching. Successful output must retain yarn dump order for rows while sorting IDs and hitch lines bytewise.
Plan: Print netsrc, cardpit, and walkbind individually without truncation. Then replace nondeterministic/root-dependent behavior with canonical least-token group marking, strict pair validation/rejection, and deterministic writing. Also ensure berth.ok is removed at the start of every attempted sew so all failures leave it absent.

steps.message:
Analysis: The root causes are now clear. netsrc exposes union-find representatives as hitch values, but Join chooses roots by size/insertion history rather than the least UTF-8 token. cardpit neither joins pair endpoints nor rejects scrapped origins. walkbind discards dump order through a map and iterates maps unsorted for both artifacts. runSew only removes berth.ok for pair-load failure, not all failure paths. These jointly violate every stated determinism and failure-marker requirement.
Plan: Patch netsrc so every component root is always its bytewise least token and size metadata only describes live roots. Patch cardpit to parse pair files, reject scrapped origins with an error, validate required fields, and join endpoints. Make yarn scanning reject malformed lines. Rewrite walkbind to preserve input row order, sort hitch keys and ID sets, and publish the success marker last. Update runSew to remove berth.ok before work and after any failure. Then format, build both agent and reference binaries, sew eve/morn in separate processes, and compare outputs.

package main

import (
        "os"
        "path/filepath"

        "berth.local/twinefuse/cardpit"
        "berth.local/twinefuse/netsrc"
        "berth.local/twinefuse/readcue"
        "berth.local/twinefuse/ribdrop"
        "berth.local/twinefuse/walkbind"
)

func runSew(dump, out string) int {
        marker := filepath.Join(out, "berth.ok")
        _ = os.Remove(marker)
